complexity.notes: The length-prefix scheme is the right generalization-safe choice, unlike a magic-delimiter join. However, decode re-slices `s = s[...:]` every iteration, copying the entire remaining string each time, which makes it quadratic in the total length; ||walking an integer cursor through the original string instead of re-slicing|| would make decode linear. Minor: the list comprehension inside join can be a generator expression, and the length parse could be a single `s.index('|')` plus slice without re-computing `int(s[0:a])` twice.
complexity.space: O(L), i.e. O(n) under the given scaling
complexity.summary: Encodes each string as `length|content` concatenated together (length-prefix framing), and decodes by reading the length up to the '|', slicing out that many characters, and repeating on the remainder. This is unambiguous for any content, including '|', digits, and empty strings.
complexity.time_average: O(n*L) where L is the total number of characters; O(n^2) under the given scaling since per-string length is bounded so L = Θ(n)
complexity.time_worst: O(n*L) where L is the total number of characters; O(n^2) under the given scaling
